lawyer:
Muhammad Nazrul Islam, Advocate ----- For the Appellant.

parties:
Islami Bank Bangladesh Ltd ------ Petitioner
vs

full_judgment: 10. Mr Mahmudul Islam, the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the contesting respondent placing the decision reported in AIR 1927 (Sind) 49 (Abdul Ali Moosabhoy vs Gokaldas Lalji and another) submits that section 73 of the Contract Act makes it compulsory for the plaintiff to prove that he has suffered damage and the extent to which he has suffered before a court can award him damages for breach of contract, and if he does not give the best evidence, every presumption should be made against him. He submits that before the trial Court the plaintiff failed to prove the quantum of damages and none deposed that the bank actually suffered damages for which claim as prayed may be entertained. He submits that the main criterion of the damages must be proved by proper and adequate evidence which is very much lacking in the present case.
